query: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has high strength at room temperature and elevated temperature but a relatively high density of 10.21 g cm−3. What single intervention could reduce its density without sacrificing its mechanical properties at room temperature and at elevated temperatures, including approximately 1000 °C? State the proposed intervention and mechanism, predict directional changes relative to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr, define the applicable temperature and loading boundaries, identify supporting prior evidence, and propose an experiment and rejection criterion that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Substituting a portion of Hf with Sc in the HfMoTaTiZr high-entropy alloy will reduce its density without sacrificing its mechanical properties at room temperature and elevated temperatures up to 1000 °C.
generation.intervention: Substitution of 10 at.% Hf with Sc
generation.conditions: Room temperature and elevated temperatures up to 1000 °C
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a solid solution with reduced lattice parameter due to the smaller atomic radius of Sc compared to Hf
generation.mechanism: The high-entropy effect promotes the formation of a solid solution, which reduces the formation of detrimental phases and enhances the mechanical properties of the alloy. The substitution of Hf with Sc reduces the overall density of the alloy due to the lower atomic mass of Sc, while the high-entropy effect maintains the mechanical properties by promoting solid solution strengthening.
generation.predicted_outcome: Based on the atomic masses of Sc and Hf, a 10 at.% substitution of Hf with Sc is expected to reduce the density by approximately 5% relative to the as-cast HfMoTaTiZr, from 10.21 g cm−3 to 9.70 g cm−3, with no significant change in yield strength and ultimate tensile strength at room temperature and 1000 °C
generation.baseline: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr high-entropy alloy with a density of 10.21 g cm−3 and yield strength of 1000 MPa at room temperature and 500 MPa at 1000 °C
generation.boundary: The alloy will be tested under uniaxial tensile loading at room temperature and 1000 °C, with a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1
generation.uncertainty: There may be uncertainties in the actual density reduction and mechanical properties of the Sc-substituted alloy due to variations in the alloy composition and processing conditions.

falsification_experiment.design: Uniaxial tensile testing and density measurement of the Sc-substituted HfMoTaTiZr alloy at room temperature and 1000 °C, with the as-cast HfMoTaTiZr alloy as a control group
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the density of the Sc-substituted alloy is not reduced by at least 3% relative to the as-cast HfMoTaTiZr, or if the yield strength or ultimate tensile strength at room temperature or 1000 °C is reduced by more than 5%, the hypothesis is falsified. The data will be analyzed using a two-way ANOVA to compare the mechanical properties of the Sc-substituted alloy with the as-cast HfMoTaTiZr alloy.
